chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'The dowry (mahr) is not obligatory except through sexual intercourse (wiqāʿ) in the private part (farj).'

key_terms.الْمَهْرَ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: When does the full dowry become obligatory in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the full dowry (mahr al-mithl or the agreed amount) is not due until actual consummation, distinguishing it from the 'partial dowry' (mahr al-nuskh) payable upon separation. This ruling underscores the legal significance of physical intimacy in validating the financial rights of the wife, a principle widely discussed by scholars like Al-Tusi in his compilation of legal precedents.
